note_on_method: Nobody working on this has played on these courts. Mecklenburg County publishes no court count for any park. It names individual numbered courts, split between reservable and open play, so each count below is the number of distinct court numbers the county names at that park, and each note quotes the county's own lines. Where the county is silent, and it is silent about lighting, surface, nets, hours and prices, the note says so rather than guessing.

slots.description:
Clarks Creek Park has eight pickleball courts, the most of any park we list in Charlotte, on Hucks Road in the north of the city. Mecklenburg County never says "eight". It lists "Clarks Creek Park: Courts 1-5" as reservable and "Clarks Creek Park: Courts 6-8" as open play, which together name courts one to eight with nothing missing and nothing counted twice.

The City of Charlotte parks layer holds three records with Clarks Creek in the title: this park at 5435 Hucks Road, Clarks Creek Nature Preserve across the road at 5434, and Clarks Creek Greenway Park on Mallard Creek Road. Only this one has pickleball.
slots.getting_there: 5435 Hucks Rd, Charlotte, NC 28269, in the north of the city. The county publishes no parking information for this park: no lot, no capacity, no restriction. It does warn that its neighbourhood parks "do not typically have parking or restroom features", but Clarks Creek is classified as a Community park, so that warning most likely does not apply. Nothing is recorded either way about parking or restrooms here.
slots.what_to_expect: Eight courts, five bookable and three always open. The county says any court not on its reservable list is "non-reservable and open to the public on a first come, first serve basis", so courts 6, 7 and 8 cannot be taken from you by a booking. It publishes nothing about the courts themselves: no lighting, no surface material, no statement about nets, and no price for the reservations it charges for. All of those read "Not stated" on this page. Charlotte is one of the cities in this directory where the operator publishes no lighting data at all, and at an eight-court site that is the gap you will feel most.

faqs.q: How many pickleball courts does Clarks Creek Park have?
faqs.a: Eight. Mecklenburg County names them individually rather than giving a total: courts 1 to 5 are reservable and courts 6 to 8 are open play, a complete run from 1 to 8 with no gaps and no court listed twice.

faqs.q: Can I play here without booking?
faqs.a: Yes, on three of the eight. Courts 6, 7 and 8 are permanently open play and cannot be reserved. That is the largest guaranteed walk-up allocation at any Charlotte park in this set.

slots.description:
Freedom Park is one of Mecklenburg County's Regional parks and one of Charlotte's best-known green spaces, and its pickleball courts are numbered 11 to 16. That is not an error. Courts 1 to 10 at Freedom Park are tennis courts, listed separately higher up the same county page, and the county runs a single numbering series across both sports at this site.

As a Regional park rather than a neighbourhood one, Freedom Park sits outside the county's blanket warning that its smaller parks lack parking and restrooms.
slots.getting_there: 2435 Cumberland Ave, Charlotte, NC 28203, south of uptown. The county publishes no parking guidance for the park and no capacity or restriction, which for a Regional park drawing visitors from across the city is a meaningful gap. Nothing on the county's courts page states whether there are restrooms at the courts themselves.
slots.what_to_expect: Six courts, four bookable and two always open, sharing a site with ten tennis courts. Expect a destination park rather than a neighbourhood one, busy in a way the court count alone does not convey. The county states that any court not on its reservable list is open on a first-come, first-served basis, so courts 13 and 16 are yours if they are free. What it does not publish is lighting, surface, nets, opening hours or the price of a reservation, so all of those read "Not stated" here. If you are looking for the courts on arrival, the numbering is your friend: the pickleball is the 11-to-16 block.

faqs.q: Why do Freedom Park's pickleball courts start at number 11?
faqs.a: Because courts 1 to 10 at the same park are tennis courts, listed separately on the county's page. Mecklenburg runs one numbering series across both sports at this site instead of restarting it, so the pickleball block begins where the tennis block ends.

faqs.q: How many pickleball courts are there, and which can I book?
faqs.a: Six, numbered 11 to 16. Courts 11, 12, 14 and 15 are reservable for a small fee; courts 13 and 16 are permanently open play. The county does not publish what the fee is.

slots.description:
Clanton Park is a Community park in south-west Charlotte with six pickleball courts, numbered 1 to 6. It sits on Clanton Road near the Revolution Park area.

The address is worth a note of its own. The commercial dataset this directory started from carries a Clanton Park row with the postcode 28208. The county's own parks layer gives 28217 for 1520 Clanton Road. The postcode published here is 28217, because it comes from the operator's record rather than from an aggregator.
slots.getting_there: 1520 Clanton Rd, Charlotte, NC 28217. No parking information is published for this park: no lot, no capacity, no restriction. The county's warning that neighbourhood parks lack parking and restrooms does not formally apply here, since Clanton is classified as a Community park, but the county publishes nothing positive about either facility at this site.
slots.what_to_expect: Six courts, four bookable and two open play. As at every Mecklenburg park in this set, the county keeps some back: courts 5 and 6 cannot be reserved by anyone, which the county describes as first come, first serve. Nothing is published about lighting, surface, nets, hours or the reservation fee, so all of those read "Not stated". The county does say generally that its local park courts "are always open for play", which is a statement about access rather than a timetable. It does not tell you when the park closes.

faqs.q: How many courts are there and which are bookable?
faqs.a: Six, numbered 1 to 6. Courts 1 to 4 are reservable for a small fee the county does not price; courts 5 and 6 are permanently open play and cannot be reserved.

faqs.q: Is this the same as Clanton Park Community Garden?
faqs.a: No. The city's parks layer holds the community garden as a separate record at a different address on Revolution Park Drive. The pickleball courts are at 1520 Clanton Road.

slots.description:
Martin Luther King Jr. Park is a Community park in west Charlotte with six pickleball courts, numbered 1 to 6. Mecklenburg County writes it "MLK Park" in its court lists and "Martin Luther King Jr. Park" in the city parks layer; the full name is published here.

The reservable split is the most scattered of the five Charlotte parks. Courts 2, 3, 5 and 6 can be booked, and courts 1 and 4 are permanently open play. The two walk-up courts are not a block at one end but spaced through the run. The two lists still rebuild a complete 1 to 6.
slots.getting_there: 2600 Ravencroft Dr, Charlotte, NC 28208. The county publishes no parking guidance, capacity or restriction for this park, and nothing about restrooms at the courts. As a Community park it falls outside the county's general warning about neighbourhood parks lacking both, but that is an inference from a size class rather than a statement about this site.
slots.what_to_expect: Six courts, four bookable and two, courts 1 and 4, always open play. The county states that any court not on its reservable list is open first come, first served, so those two cannot be taken by a booking. Everything else about the courts is unpublished: no lighting, so evening play cannot be confirmed; no surface material; no statement about nets; no opening hours; and no price for the reservations. All read "Not stated" here.

faqs.q: Is this the same as Martin Luther King Jr. Middle School?
faqs.a: No. The city's parks layer holds the middle school as a separate record on Bilmark Avenue. The park with the pickleball courts is at 2600 Ravencroft Drive.

faqs.q: Does the county publish opening hours?
faqs.a: Not for this park or any other. It says only that its local park courts "are always open for play", which describes access rather than a timetable. It does not tell you when the park gates close, so hours are recorded as not stated.

slots.description:
Colonel Francis J. Beatty Park is the smallest pickleball site we list in Charlotte at three courts, and the only one where a walk-up player is competing for a single court. Mecklenburg County lists courts 2 and 3 as reservable and court 1 as open play, so exactly one of the three can never be booked.

Beatty also appears on the county's tennis lists, with courts 5 and 6 reservable and court 4 as open play, so the site runs one numbering series across both sports: pickleball is 1 to 3 and tennis is 4 to 6. It is a Regional park, the county's largest size class, in the far south-east of the city.
slots.getting_there: 4330 Weddington Rd, Charlotte, NC 28105, in the far south-east of the city near Matthews. If you are searching for it, expect listings to place it in Matthews on the strength of the postcode; the park itself is inside the Charlotte city limits. The county publishes no parking guidance, capacity or restriction for the park, and nothing about restrooms at the courts.
slots.what_to_expect: Three courts, two bookable and one always open. That ratio matters more here than anywhere else in Charlotte: if both reservable courts are booked, a walk-up player is waiting for court 1 alone. The county publishes no lighting, surface, nets, hours or reservation price, so all of those read "Not stated". The site also carries three tennis courts numbered 4 to 6, sharing the same numbering series, so if you are looking at signage on arrival the pickleball is the 1-to-3 end.

faqs.q: Is this park in Charlotte or Matthews?
faqs.a: Charlotte, though it takes a third source to settle it. The postcode 28105 is a Matthews mailing ZIP and many listings place the park there, while the City of Charlotte parks layer labels its city as Charlotte. The US Census geocoder places the park's published coordinates inside the incorporated place of Charlotte, in Mecklenburg County.

faqs.q: What are my chances of getting a court without booking?
faqs.a: Lower than anywhere else in Charlotte. Only court 1 is guaranteed open play, so if both bookable courts are reserved there is one court for every walk-up. Clarks Creek Park keeps three courts back and is the better bet if you have not booked.
